rawFindings.title: Missing modelName fallback breaks population for ad-hoc structures
rawFindings.explanation: The original code provided a fallback for modelName using model.modelName if options.model and schema.options.ref were undefined, allowing population to work for ad-hoc structures without explicit schema references. The new code removes this fallback, so if neither options.model nor schema.options.ref is provided, it throws an error, breaking existing users relying on model.modelName fallback.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the fallback to model.modelName in the modelName assignment to avoid breaking population for ad-hoc structures, e.g.: var modelName = options.model || (schema && schema.options.ref) || model.modelName;

rawFindings.title: Tests now incorrectly expect an error where none was previously thrown
rawFindings.explanation: The changed test asserts that an error is expected (assert.ok(err)) whereas the original test asserts no error (assert.ifError(err)). Without a corresponding lib code change supporting error expectation behavior, this may cause previously passing tests to fail unnecessarily.
rawFindings.suggestion: Review the related code to verify if expecting an error is correct; if population is now supposed to throw an error for missing modelName, keep test change. Otherwise, revert test assertion to assert.ifError(err);

rawFindings.title: Similar incorrect expectation of error in populate model test
rawFindings.explanation: This test now expects an error (assert.ok(err)) where previously no error was expected (assert.ifError(err)). This might cause false test failures if the underlying code change does not intend to introduce an error on this case.
rawFindings.suggestion: Verify that the error is the expected new behavior due to modelName resolution change; if not, revert the test to assert.ifError(err).
